title: VF-018: objects.Kernel#price's output relation under JBMC and auto --confirm with an 1800 s limit (closes VF-018 with its three sibling jobs)
description: Closes VF-018 (verification/findings.md) when this job and its three siblings pass. The ignored test the_output_relations_have_the_same_verdicts_under_jbmc_and_auto_confirm in lib/tests/heap.rs failed in job 20261107-080218 because JBMC did not finish objects.Kernel#price's output relation within the test's own 600 s limit (the default timeout_seconds of the options), where the own checker proves it. By the user's decision 6 of llm-dlc/loops/cleanup.md, the only change is a longer limit: the JBMC tests in heap.rs now take it from JVMCONTRACT_HEAP_TIME_LIMIT (600 s when unset; the own checker's runs keep 600), and this job sets it to 1800. The test and its expectations are unchanged. If it fails, VF-018 is deferred to the user with no second attempt. In 20261107-080218, two runs timed out (objects.Kernel#price's output relation under --engine jbmc and under auto --confirm) and the rest took about 2 minutes, so the worst case here is about 2 x 30 min + 5 min, plus the release build.
expected: exits 0: the ignored test the_output_relations_have_the_same_verdicts_under_jbmc_and_auto_confirm passes unchanged with JVMCONTRACT_HEAP_TIME_LIMIT=1800. Under both engines, the two after-build checks Verified and the three others Violation, each violation's witness run on a JVM.

resources.notes: a release build, then about 10 JBMC runs; at 600 s two of them timed out (20261107-080218 ran 21-23 min at 1.2 GiB peak), so up to two 30 min runs now, JBMC's memory growing with its time

steps.name: the_output_relations_have_the_same_verdicts_under_jbmc_and_auto_confirm with a 1800 s limit
steps.run: cd lib && JVMCONTRACT_HEAP_TIME_LIMIT=1800 cargo test --release --test heap -- --ignored the_output_relations_have_the_same_verdicts_under_jbmc_and_auto_confirm --exact
